instruction: Download each open blog post in Chrome as a PDF, name the files by their titles, and save them to /home/user/Documents/Blog for offline reading.

metadata.explanation: Task requires downloading exactly 2 blog articles as PDFs to /home/user/Documents/Blog and naming them by their titles. Evaluator verifies exactly 2 PDF files exist with filenames matching expected title patterns ('agent' and 'human-data-quality'). Custom getter lists all PDF files with metadata, metric checks both count and filename patterns using fuzzy matching. Full credit (1.0) for correct count and matching filenames, partial credit for count-only or partial matches.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 1.0 for exactly 2 PDFs with correct title-based filenames, 0.7-0.99 for correct count with partial filename matches, 0.3 for correct count but wrong filenames, 0.3-0.5 for wrong count

llm_judge_reasons: Complete semantic coverage: Evaluator correctly checks both PDF count (exactly 2) AND filename patterns matching blog post titles
Getter logic is sound: Uses find command to list all PDF files in target directory with filenames and count
Metric logic is robust: Verifies exact count first, then checks filenames contain expected title patterns ('agent', 'human-data-quality') using fuzzy keyword matching with 50% threshold
Expected values are semantically correct: Title patterns accurately reflect the blog post URLs (agent from 'agent/', human-data-quality from 'human-data-quality/')
Scoring logic is appropriate: Full credit (1.0) for correct count + all patterns matched, partial credit for count-only or partial pattern matches, scaled appropriately for edge cases
Parameter handling is correct: Metric properly accesses rules dict directly as expected parameter (expected.get('exact_count'), expected.get('expected_title_patterns'))
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts filenames → Metric compares against expected count and patterns → Returns appropriate score
